business_model.basis: Stated in P3 (10-K MD&A) and shown as the only revenue line in F2 (10-Q income statement)
business_model.claim: Granite Ridge's sole revenue source is the sale of oil and natural gas produced from its working interests in wells it participates in alongside third-party operators.
quotes: We derive our revenues from our interests in the sale of oil and natural gas production.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1 Business, Marketing and Customers section)
business_model.claim: Production is marketed and sold by third-party operating partners to energy marketing companies, refineries and their affiliates; the company does not sell directly to end buyers.
quotes: We generally rely on our operating partners to market and sell our production.

Our exposures to credit risk, in part, are through receivables resulting from the sale of our oil and natural gas production, which operating partners market on our behalf to energy marketing companies, refineries, and their affiliates.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1 Business, Assets of Granite Ridge section)
business_model.claim: The company operates through two distinct models: Operated Partnerships (majority capital, significant control over strategy and rig schedules) and Traditional Non-Operated Assets (minority interests, proportionate participation).
quotes: Operated partnerships are comprised of transactions where Granite Ridge makes controlled investments with proven teams in their area of expertise. Traditional non-operated assets are comprised of minority interests in core areas managed by experienced operators.

In these partnerships, we account for a significant majority of the capital at risk, so we have significant control over acquisition costs and strategy, development costs, timing and rig schedules, and well design.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K) and reiterated in P4 (10-Q MD&A)
business_model.claim: Assets are spread across six U.S. unconventional basins—Permian, Eagle Ford, Bakken, Haynesville, DJ, and Appalachian—providing geographic and hydrocarbon diversification.
quotes: We hold assets in the Permian (Delaware and Midland basins), Eagle Ford, Bakken, Haynesville, Denver-Julesburg ("DJ") and Appalachian basins (collectively, our "Properties").
We aim to deliver a diversified portfolio with best-in-class full cycle returns by investing in a large number of high-graded opportunities developed by proven public and private operators.

business_model.basis: Stated in P4 (10-Q MD&A) and P3 (10-K MD&A); the 60%, 17%, 37% figures are stated in P4
business_model.claim: Revenue is driven primarily by two variables: production volumes (oil MBbl and natural gas MMcf) and realized commodity prices (oil per Bbl, natural gas per Mcf), which in turn track NYMEX benchmarks plus or minus a regional differential.
quotes: Our revenues vary from year to year primarily due to changes in realized commodity prices and production volumes.
The price at which our oil and natural gas production is sold typically reflects either a premium or discount to the NYMEX benchmark price.

business_model.basis: Stated in P3 (10-K MD&A cost structure section) and shown as line items in F2 (10-Q income statement)
business_model.claim: The principal cost drivers are lease operating expenses, production and ad valorem taxes, depletion and accretion, general and administrative expenses, interest expense, and gains or losses on commodity derivatives.
quotes: Lease operating expenses are the costs incurred in the operation of producing properties, including workover costs.
Depletion and accretion include the systematic expensing of the capitalized costs incurred to acquire, explore and develop oil and natural gas.

business_model.basis: Inferred from the absence of segment reporting in F1, F2, F3, P1, P3, P4; basin-level data is explicitly tabulated
business_model.claim: The company does not report formal operating segments; instead, production, reserves and costs are disclosed by basin (Permian, Eagle Ford, Bakken, Haynesville, DJ, Appalachian) and by product type (oil vs. natural gas).

business_model.basis: Stated in F2 (10-Q income statement) and explained in P3 (10-K MD&A, Gain/(Loss) on Derivatives section)
business_model.claim: Commodity derivative hedging can swing reported GAAP earnings from profit to loss: in Q3 2026 a $(52,698) thousand derivative loss turned positive net operating income of $59,260 thousand into a net loss of $(10,051) thousand, whereas in Q3 2025 a $5,224 thousand derivative gain contributed to a $14,523 thousand net income.
